prompt: In many countries, fewer school leavers are choosing to study science and mathematics at a higher level. Why is this happening? What could be done to encourage more young people into these subjects?
essay:
Nowadays, in a lot of countries the number of the students who choose science and mathematics in higher level is going down. In this essay I will discuss the reasons of this problem and also suggest some solutions.

Firstly, the main reason is that these subjects are very difficult. Mathematics and physics need a lot of practice and many students think they can not get good marks in them. If a student choose a difficult subject and fail the exam, his average will be low and he can not enter to a good university. In my country, for example, many of my friends changed from physics to economics because of this. So many students prefer easier subjects like business or media, which are not so difficult.

Secondly, another reason is the way of teaching. In many schools the teacher only explain the theory from the book and give a lot of homework, so the students become bored. They do not see how science is connected with real life. Moreover, some students think that science jobs are not paid well comparing with business jobs, so they do not want to spend many years for studying such a difficult subject.

To solve this problem, the governments should give scholarships for the science students. Also the schools should make the lessons more interesting with experiments.

In conclusion, students avoid science and mathematics because these subjects are difficult and the teaching is boring, and I think the government and the schools should take some action about this problem as soon as possible.
title: Why fewer school leavers study science and maths
